login.title: Sign in to ASAPify
login.lede: Manage regional notifications. Operators also get map and decision access.
login.note: Demo: you sign in without an account, and all data inside is fictional.
login.rule_t: How a peat region is rated
login.rule: Every hour, the rules engine reads three inputs per region: ΔT (land surface temperature against its 2021–2025 baseline), air humidity and cloud cover. Alert calls an AI agent that checks NASA FIRMS hotspots, and an operator decides what goes out.
about.title: Early warning for peatland fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan
about.lede: ASAPify checks 65 peat regions every 15 minutes for new NASA data: how much warmer the land surface is than usual for that hour and season, how dry the air is, and whether clouds hide the ground. A rules engine rates each region; when one reaches Alert, an AI agent checks NASA FIRMS fire hotspots, and an operator decides whether subscribers in that province are told.
about.scope: Coverage: peat in 11 provinces of Sumatra and Kalimantan, as 65 NASA POWER grid cells (0.5° × 0.625°) that each hold at least 25 km² of mapped peat. The inputs arrive 2–3 days late, so ASAPify shows recent conditions, not a live fire feed.
about.name: The name comes from asap, Indonesian for smoke.
about.step1_d: NASA POWER hourly skin temperature and humidity, and Open-Meteo cloud cover. Every value carries its source, unit, time and quality: accepted, degraded or rejected. Rejected data never reaches the rules.
about.step2_d: ΔT = skin temperature minus the mean of the same UTC hour, ±15 days, in 2021–2025. Both sides are the same measurement from the same source.
about.step3_d: Trapezoid memberships turn ΔT and humidity into a utility for Safe, Warning and Alert. The highest wins; within 0.05 the more severe one does. Cloud above 60 % means Not observable. Every change of status is recorded.
about.step4_d: On entering Alert, or when an operator asks, a Gemini agent built with Google ADK calls fetch_firms_data for VIIRS hotspots and answers Confirmed, Rejected or Needs manual review in YAML. The backend checks its numbers against what the tool returned.
about.step5_d: The operator publishes or rejects each verification. Only published alerts reach subscribers who chose that province, by Telegram DM and in the web inbox.
about.ai_rule: The status comes only from the data and the rules. The AI agent reads evidence for the operator and cannot change a status.
about.st_warning: Medium anomaly (about 3–6 K). Closer monitoring; no agent call.
about.st_noobs: Cloud cover above 60 % or an input missing. Never counted as safe.
about.limit1: One NASA POWER cell covers about 55 × 70 km, so a small fire can disappear in the average.
about.limit2: Skin temperature and humidity are reanalysis estimates, and cloud cover is a weather-model estimate, not a satellite cloud mask.
about.limit3: The inputs are 2–3 days behind real time.
about.limit4: A FIRMS hotspot is a thermal detection, not proof of fire. No imagery is checked, so the agent never claims that smoke was seen.
about.limit5: The peat map in use (KHG) is incomplete, so some peat areas are not monitored yet.
about.data_note: All processing runs on Google Cloud: Cloud Run, Cloud Scheduler, Firestore, Vertex AI (Gemini) and the Agent Development Kit.
about.src_power: Hourly skin temperature (TS) and relative humidity (RH2M), 0.5° × 0.625°, about 2–3 days behind
about.src_firms: NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 near-real-time hotspots, 375 m, fetched by the agent during verification
